{{Short description|Japanese chemist and emeritus professor}}
{{nihongo|'''Haruo Hosoya'''|細矢 治夫|Hosoya Haruo|born 1936|lead=yes}} is a Japanese [[chemist]] and [[emeritus professor]] of [[Ochanomizu University]], [[Tokyo]], Japan. He is the namesake of the [[Hosoya index]] used in [[discrete mathematics]] and [[computational chemistry]].<ref name=croat>[https://hrcak.srce.hr/clanak/19756 "Haruo Hosoya"], by [[Ante Graovac]], ''Croatica Chemica Acta'' 80 (2) XXI–XXII (2007)</ref>

== Early life ==
Hosoya was born in [[Kamakura, Kanagawa|Kamakura]], [[Japan]] to a family of an office worker. During 1955-1959 he studied at the [[University of Tokyo]]. In 1964 he wrote his [[Ph.D.]] thesis, "Study on the Structure of Reactive Intermediates and Reaction Mechanism". 

== Career ==
After postdoc work abroad ([[Ann Arbor]], [[Michigan]], with prof. [[John R. Platt|John Platt]]), in 1969 he became [[associate professor]] at the Ochanomizu University, where he worked for 33 years until his retirement in 2002. After retirement he has kept working in computational chemistry.<ref name="croat" />

In 1971, Hosoya defined the [[topological index]] (a [[graph invariant]]) now known as the Hosoya index as the total number of [[Matching (graph theory)|matchings]] of a graph plus 1.<ref>Hosoya H., Bull. Chem. Soc. Jpn., 44, 1971, 2332</ref> The Hosoya index is often used in [[Mathematical chemistry|computer (mathematical)]] chemistry investigations for organic compounds.

In 2002-2003 the  ''[[Internet Electronic Journal of Molecular Design]]'' dedicated a series of issues to commemorate the 65th birthday of professor Hosoya.<ref>Special issues dedicated to Professor Haruo Hosoya on the occasion of the 65th birthday, Internet Electronic Journal of Molecular Design, [https://www.biochempress.com/cv01_i09.html 2002, vol 1 no. 9] &mdash; [https://www.biochempress.com/cv02_i06.html 2003, Volume 2, Number 6]).</ref>

Hosoya's article  "The Topological Index Z Before and After 1971" describes the history of the notion and the associated inside stories and details other Hosoya's achievements.<ref name=before>Hosoya H., ''[https://www.biochempress.com/av01_0428.html The Topological Index Z Before and After 1971]'', ''Internet Electronic Journal of Molecular Design'', 2002, 1, 428–442</ref>

Hosoya also introduced the triangle of numbers known as [[Hosoya's triangle]] (originally "Fibonacci triangle", but that name can be ambiguous).<ref>Haruo Hosoya, "Fibonacci Triangle", ''[[The Fibonacci Quarterly]]'', vol. 14, no. 2 (1976), pp. 173–178.</ref>
